project: LiH VQE Custom Circuit Design Test with PySCF Control
description: Test Ralph's ability to MANUALLY DESIGN variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) circuits for LiH molecule at 2.0 Å bond length. This test focuses on using PySCF for active orbital control and FCI reference energy calculation, ensuring chemical interpretation.

objectives.description: MANUALLY DESIGN and implement a VQE circuit for LiH molecule at 2.0 Å bond length. Use PySCF to control active orbital selection with chemical interpretation (active_space=(2,3)), perform parity transformation to 4 qubits. Compute FCI reference energy using PySCF.
acceptance_criteria: Python script that uses PySCF to define LiH molecule with bond length 2.0 Å, basis set STO-3G
Use PySCF to select active orbitals with chemical interpretation for active space (2 electrons, 3 orbitals)
Implement parity transformation using Tencirchem to obtain 4-qubit Hamiltonian
Compute FCI energy using PySCF as reference energy
MANUALLY DESIGN VQE ansatz circuit: DO NOT use pre-defined ansatz functions like HEA.ry(), UCCSD(), etc.
Manually construct quantum circuit using basic quantum gates (Rx, Ry, Rz, CNOT, etc.) with trainable parameters
Document the circuit design rationale and architecture choices
Use Scipy BFGS optimizer for classical optimization
Track and record energy convergence curve during optimization
Compute final VQE energy and compare with PySCF FCI reference
Output circuit gates, parameters, energy curve, and final energy
Generate lih_results.json file with structured results
Run validation script to verify implementation
Documentation explaining the VQE setup, circuit design, and results
Ralph learning log documenting iterative learning and design decisions

lih_fci_reference_note.description: FCI energy reference must be computed using PySCF, not taken from fixed benchmark
lih_fci_reference_note.note: Ralph should compute FCI energy for LiH at 2.0 Å with active_space=(2,3) using PySCF's CASCI or FCI implementation. This computed FCI energy serves as reference for VQE accuracy.

molecular_settings.active_orbital_selection: Use PySCF to select active orbitals with chemical interpretation (e.g., energy ordering, HOMO-LUMO). Do NOT use fixed orbital indices.

vqe_settings.ansatz_design: MANUAL DESIGN REQUIRED - NO PRE-DEFINED ANSATZ FUNCTIONS
prohibited_approaches: DO NOT use pre-defined ansatz functions: HEA.ry(), HEA.rx(), HEA.ucc(), UCC(), UCCSD(), etc.
DO NOT call any function that returns a complete ansatz circuit
DO NOT use 'from_xxx' methods that construct ansatz automatically
manual_construction_required: Manually add parameterized gates to the circuit
Manually construct entanglement layers if needed

orbital_selection_requirements: Use PySCF to perform Hartree-Fock calculation for LiH
Select active orbitals based on chemical interpretation (e.g., energy ordering, natural orbitals)
Active space must contain 2 electrons in 3 orbitals
Orbital selection should be justified (e.g., HOMO, LUMO, LUMO+1)
Document the selected orbital indices and their energies
fci_reference_requirements: Compute FCI energy using PySCF's CASCI or FCI implementation
Use the computed FCI energy as reference for VQE accuracy target
Document FCI calculation method and energy value
circuit_design_requirements: Circuit must have trainable parameters (at least 4 parameters)
Circuit should include both single-qubit rotations and entangling gates
No restriction on total gate count (can use as many gates as needed)
Circuit depth should be reasonable for 4-qubit system
Document design choices: why certain gates, connectivity, layers were chosen
output_requirements: Clean, well-commented code showing manual circuit construction
Clear output showing VQE optimization progress
Reproducible results (set random seeds if needed)
Detailed documentation of circuit design approach and rationale
Ralph learning log showing iterative learning and design decisions

verification_points: FCI energy must be computed using PySCF (not taken from fixed benchmark)
